AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 17, 2019
REGULAR MEETING
  6:15 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Margarita L. Rios, Mayor
  Luigi Vernola, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Leonard Shryock, Councilmember
 Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
 the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
 subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
 minutes.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
 certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
 matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
 meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
 devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
 documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
 Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
 that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
 has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
 during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
 telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

ROLL CALL
   Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk Association of Management Employees.

  II.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk City Employees Association.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8054-016-020; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: Liberty Utilities; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

  IV.  PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 54957(b)(1); TITLE: CITY
  ATTORNEY.

  V.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8045-008-902; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: State of California; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

INVOCATION
  April Reutter
  Director of Pray Norwalk

FLAG SALUTE
  Natalia Ochoa, 8th grade
  Lakeside Middle School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  Recognition of 2019 Back to School Student Headstart project sponsors.

  II.  Recognition of the 2019 Home & Business Beautification Contest Winners.

  III.  City Council to declare September as National Hispanic Heritage Month in the City of Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  Paint the Town Pink.

  2.  Special Recognition of Public Services and Public Safety staff.
   3.  Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department Town Hall meeting highlights.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of
  September 3, 7, and 10, 2019. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period August 11, 2019 –
  August 24, 2019, in the total amount of $920,434.36. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  August 28, through September 10, 2019, in the total amount of $1,462,882.96. 640

  Report

  4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Breanna
  Gonzales, Raul Alejandro Lopez, and Jovita Torna. 830-07/12/20

  Report

  5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – SEPTEMBER 11, 2019 - No action is required unless the City
  Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Synopsis

  6.  PROJECT NO. 7357- ACCEPT WORK FOR THE INSTALLATION OF CHAIN LINK FENCING ON
  ACQUIRED TANK FARM PROPERTY ADJACENT TO HOLIFIELD PARK, ENGINEERS REPORT NO.
  19-22 - Staff recommends City Council accept the work of Alcorn Fence Company of Sun Valley in the
  amount of $34,069.50 for Project No. 7357, the installation of chain link fencing on acquired Tank Farm
  property adjacent to Holifield Park. 1004-05-7357

  Report

  7.  PROJECT NO. 3302-1920 - AWARD OF CONTRACT FOR ANNUAL CITYWIDE SIDEWALK
  CONCRETE REPAIR AND REPLACEMENT, ENGINEER’S REPORT NO. 19-23 - Staff recommends
  City Council award a contract to CT&T Concrete Paving, Inc. of Diamond Bar in the amount of
  $260,250 for Project No. 3302-1920, citywide sidewalk concrete repair and replacement; and authorize
  the City Manager to execute the agreement and any extension/amendments including potential change
  orders, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City
  Attorney. 1005-04-3302-1920

  Report

  8.  AGREEMENTS – NORWALK-LA MIRADA UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT MASTER RECREATIONAL
  USE AGREEMENT AND INDIVIDUAL SITE RECREATIONAL USE AGREEMENTS FOR RAMONA
  PARK, NEW RIVER PARK, LOS ALISOS MIDDLE SCHOOL AND DOLLAND ELEMENTARY
  SCHOOL - Staff recommends City Council approve agreements with the Norwalk-La Mirada Unified
  School District for an updated Master Recreational Use Agreement and Individual Site Recreational
  Use Agreements for Ramona Park, New River Park, Los Alisos Middle School, and Dolland Elementary
  School for a period of ten years with an option to extend for five years; and authorize the City Manager
  to execute the agreements and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of
  the City, in forms approved by the City Attorney. 530-04/530-04-02
   Report

APPOINTMENTS

  9.  ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARING

  10. RESOLUTION NO. 19-49 – PETITION FOR ESTABLISHMENT OF PREFERENTIAL PARKING ZONE
  – NORTH SIDE OF EXCELSIOR DRIVE, BETWEEN STUDEBAKER ROAD AND ELMCROFT
  AVENUE – Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-49, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK SETTING FORTH ITS FINDING OF FACT AND
  APPROVING THE INSTALLATION OF THE PREFERENTIAL PARKING ZONE FOR THE NORTH
  SIDE OF EXCELSIOR DRIVE, BETWEEN STUDEBAKER ROAD AND ELMCROFT AVENUE. 1050-
  02-02

  Report

REPORTS

  11. RESOLUTION NO. 19-54 – BUDGET AMENDMENT - PRINTING AND POSTAGE COSTS FOR THE
  FALL AND WINTER SCHEDULE ACTIVITIES BROCHURE - Staff recommends City Council adopt
  Resolution No. 19-54, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AUTHORIZING AN ADMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 ADOPTED BUDGET TO
  TRANSFER FUNDS TO COVER COSTS FOR PRINTING AND MAILING THE FALL AND WINTER
  2019 SCHEDULE OF ACTIVITIES BROCHURES TO ALL NORWALK RESIDENTS, in the amount of
  $84,000. 610

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated September 13, 2019.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
